catalog_quote: [p.93] Because each word has its own stress, there are actually three stressed syllables in each of these pause groups. However, one syllable in each pause group (/ka/, /a/ and /ti/) has an additional stress. ... 3. STRESS GROUP (PHONOLOGICAL WORD) A stress group consists of a group of 1-3 syllables, but 4-6 syllable stress groups occur frequently in verbs. Stress occurs on the last high tone or on the first syllable if there are [no] highs. 3.1 One-Syllable One-syllable stress groups carry stress with both high and low tone. ... [p.94] 3.2 Multi-Syllable Two-syllable stress groups carry stress on the last high tone, or on the first syllable if there are no highs. (H-H) ... (H-L) ... (L-H) ... (L-L) ... tone_statements.citation: Donohue, Mark. 1997. Tone systems in New Guinea. Linguistic Typology 1(3): 347-386. doi:10.1515/lity.1997.1.3.347
tone_statements.quote: Sikaritai tonal system consists of two tones, high (H) and low (L), [with] each syllable in the word assigned a tone independent of the other [syl]lables in the word (Martin 1991). The addition of affixing morphology [ap]pears to have no effect on the tones in the root, the affixes having their [own t]one and there appearing to be no tone sandhi rules operating.

tone_statements.summary: Two syllable-level tones, high and low, freely combined, unaffected by affixation and without sandhi. A secondary summary of Martin 1991 that matches the entry.
